newsitem.title: USA: Florida tobacco trial suspended until Monday.
newsitem.headline: Florida tobacco trial suspended until Monday.

text.p: A juror fell ill Friday at the trial of a wrongful-death suit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, and the judge ordered that testimony of a key plaintiff witness resume on Monday.
Circuit Court Judge Bernard Knachman sent the jury home early for weekend. He said he would put off until Monday a decision on whether to replace the ill juror.

When court was suspended, Dr. Allan Feingold, a pulmonary specialist, was testifying on behalf of the family of Jean Connor, a 49-year-old woman and long-time smoker who died of lung cancer two years ago.
Connor's family is suing R.J. Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
